items.title: Albert Jiles Interview, 1960-06-15
items.q: Because Old Man Robichaud was the first man I understand that I heard that played a bass drum in New Orleans in the street.

ctx.x: Well, I was asking a little bit more about your Uncle Clay then. Do you remember which brass bands he played with? You mentioned your father came down and played with Onward and different bands.

Well, he played with the Salsa and occasionally with Moe's, every brass band in existence because he was a good drummer and anytime they had a chance to use him they would always try to get Clay Gile. Because Old Man Robichaud was the first man I understand that I heard that played a bass drum in New Orleans in the street. Joe Robichaud, he was a violin band.
Not a John Robichaud. John Robichaud. The old man, the violin. Yeah, yeah, yeah. Left-handed violin. Yeah, that's right. Yeah, that's right.
